01Control Valve FundamentalsDAY 1+
  • Control valve function and operating principles
  • Gate, Globe, rotary and Diaphragm valves
  • Application of different valves.
  • Single-port and double-port designs
  • Valve body, trim, stem, packing, bonnet, and seat
  • Normally open, normally closed, and fail-safe positions
02Flow Characteristics and Control PerformanceDAY 1+
  • Inherent versus installed characteristics
  • Linear, equal-percentage, and quick-opening trims
  • Rangeability and turndown
  • Valve authority and controllability
  • Cavitation, flashing, noise, and vibration
  • Effects of piping reducers and fittings
03Process Data and Sizing FundamentalsDAY 2+
  • Required process inputs and operating cases
  • Liquid, gas, steam, and two-phase flow considerations
  • Density, specific gravity, viscosity, molecular weight and compressibility
  • Flow rate, inlet pressure, outlet pressure, temperature and pressure drop
  • Unit conversions and dimensional consistency
  • Minimum, normal, maximum and start-up cases
04Control Valve Sizing CalculationsDAY 2+
  • Liquid sizing using Cv and Kv
  • Gas and steam sizing
  • Choked flow and critical pressure ratio
  • Liquid pressure recovery and piping geometry factors
  • Reynolds number and viscosity correction
  • Required versus selected valve capacity
  • Manual calculations versus software verification
05Valve, Actuator and Accessory SelectionDAY 3+
  • Valve body size versus line size
  • Body and trim materials, pressure class and end connections
  • Pneumatic diaphragm and piston actuators
  • Spring return, air failure and position failure
  • Smart positioners, I/P converters, solenoid valves and limit switches
  • Actuator thrust, torque and seating requirements
  • Control valve versus ESD valve requirements
06Advanced Applications and StandardsDAY 3+
  • Anti-cavitation and low-noise trim
  • High-pressure-drop and severe-service applications
  • Cryogenic, corrosive, erosive and high-temperature services
  • Control valve noise prediction and mitigation
  • IEC 60534 and ISA 75.01,… guidance
  • Pressure-temperature ratings and applicable material standards
  • Inspection, testing and documentation requirements
07Sizing Software WorkshopDAY 4+
  • Create a valve sizing case
  • Enter process conditions and fluid properties
  • Run minimum, normal and maximum operating cases
  • Review calculated capacity, opening, velocity and noise
  • Select valve series, trim, actuator and accessories
  • Generate and check sizing reports
  • Investigate common sizing errors
08EPC Project Deliverables and CapstoneDAY 4+
  • Control valve datasheets and specifications
  • Valve sizing calculation sheets
  • Technical bid evaluation (TBE)
  • Vendor document review
  • P&ID and instrument index coordination
  • Final project: size, select, document and defend three valves

COURSE QUESTIONS

Before you join.

Who is this course for?

Process specialists and engineers, instrumentation and control engineers, and mechanical engineers. Basic process engineering and instrumentation knowledge is recommended.

How long is the course?

The course lasts 32 training hours over four days. The day-by-day module allocation shown here is suggested.

What will I work on?

The final project brings together sizing, selection and documentation for three valves, including technical bid evaluation and vendor document review.

Where can I find dates and fees?

Dates, delivery format, fees and availability have not been published. The enrollment section lets you prepare an inquiry; a draft is not a confirmed booking.
